# TrustyStepper

`Navigation` · composition depth: `base`

Progress through a task that runs over several steps. Each step shows its number — or an icon — with a title and an optional description, and 'v-model' carries the step the user is on, 1-based. By default progress is linear: only the steps already reached and the one straight after can be picked, and the rest read as locked. The strip shows progress and moves between steps; the content of each step lives outside the component, keyed off 'v-model'.

**Use it when**
- one task splits into ordered steps and the user needs to see where they are and how much is left
- a form is long enough to break into stages the user submits at the end

**Don't use it for**
- peer views the user flips between in any order: use TrustyTabs
- paging through a list of results: use TrustyPagination
- a single yes/no stage, or one that fits on one screen: just show the form
- a read-only status timeline nobody navigates: render a plain list

```ts
import { TrustyStepper } from '@louislp/trusty-ui'
```

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `steps` | `{ title: string; description?: string \| undefined; icon?: `${string}:${string}` \| undefined; disabled?: boolean \| undefined; warning?: boolean \| undefined; }[]` | *required* | The steps, in order. Their position is their number — step 1 is the first entry — which is what `v-model` reports. Each step: - `title`: the step's name; its accessible name is "Step <n>: <title>" - `description`: second line under the title - `icon`: icon name (Iconify `collection:icon`, e.g. `ph:gear`) shown in place of the number - `disabled`: this step can never be reached, whatever the progress - `warning`: yellow dot on the indicator — something here needs attention |
| `orientation` | `"horizontal" \| "vertical"` | `"horizontal"` |  |
| `linear` | `boolean` | `true` | Sequential progress: only steps already reached, plus the one straight after, can be picked. Turn it off to let every step be picked at any time. |
| `modelValue` | `number` | — |  |

## Events

- `update:modelValue` — `[value: number \| undefined]`

## Examples in Storybook

- Default — The current step and the ones behind it are filled; step 3 is reachable, and the steps beyond it stay locked.
- Vertical — The rail runs down the side — arrow keys go up/down.
- TitlesOnly — Titles alone, when the step names carry the whole story.
- Icons — Icons replace the numbers when each step has a recognisable subject.
- Warning — A yellow (warning) dot marks a step holding something the user has to come back to.
- NonLinear — `linear: false` — every step is reachable, in any order.
- DisabledStep — A step that can never be reached, wherever progress has got to.
- Controlled — Driven from outside: the buttons move the same `v-model` the strip does.
